headline: Shares of Oracle, Broadcom, Nvidia and other AI-linked companies fell on 8 October after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's yearly sales pace is about $20 billion lower than earlier figures suggested.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: a large one-day move in AI shares, but the gap is largely a counting difference and OpenAI has not commented.
importance_line: Shareholders in these AI companies lost value on the day, and the move shows how much their prices lean on OpenAI's reported growth; the gap is largely about how sales are counted and OpenAI has not commented, so it does not by itself prove weaker demand.
summary: AI News Desk summary of reporting by the Financial Times, as relayed by Stocktwits and BeInCrypto: OpenAI told investors its annualised revenue (recent sales scaled up to a full year) was about $50 billion at the end of September, roughly $20 billion below the $70 billion figure widely reported earlier, and Oracle fell more than 5%, Broadcom nearly 4% and Nvidia more than 2% on 8 Oct 2026. The gap largely reflects different counting methods, since Anthropic's figure includes sales through cloud partners and OpenAI's does not, and OpenAI declined to comment.
notes: CNBC original blocked (Akamai error page); Quartz and Seeking Alpha also unreadable. Facts come from Stocktwits (TradingView) and the Bloomberg text read for C07-03; the BeInCrypto text read for C07-06 gives the share falls. First reporter is the Financial Times (not read directly).
